title: Calling
definition: Calling is God's summons through the Gospel by which sinners are invited and commanded to come to Christ.
summary: Calling highlights God's summons through the Gospel, by which sinners are invited and commanded to come to Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls the weary, the guilty, and the lost to come to Him for salvation and rest.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Calling is God's summons through the Gospel. Scripture does not present salvation as a private idea people discover on their own, but as good news announced by God through His Word, His messengers, and the witness of His people.

This calling comes with mercy and authority. Sinners are invited to come to Christ, but they are also commanded to repent and believe because the King Himself is speaking.

The Gospel call points directly to Jesus, who says, 'Come to me,' to the weary and burdened. Every faithful sermon, witness, and invitation should echo that call by placing Christ before sinners as Savior, Lord, and rest.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People do not need vague religious encouragement; they need to hear God's summons to come to Christ. It corrects the idea that salvation is merely a personal improvement plan and reminds the Church that evangelism is a serious, loving invitation from God Himself.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Treat the Gospel as a real call, not a soft suggestion. Respond personally to Christ, and when you teach, preach, or witness, call people plainly to repent, believe, and come to Jesus rather than only offering general spiritual comfort.
